items.title: Tribunal has gone haywire: Supreme Court slams APTEL for ignoring binding precedent
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday set aside an order of the Appellate Tribunal for Electricity (APTEL) which reviewed and reversed the tribunal's own five-year-old decision on an issue already settled by the top court. A Bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran said that such a decision, which amounted to gross breach of judicial discipline, raised serious doubts in the mind of the bench about the independence of the tribunal. "It is not often, but we do come across orders akin to the one impugned, which is in blatant breach of judicial discipline and in clear violation of Article 141 of the Constitution of India. It raises serious doubts in our minds about independence vis-à-vis accountability," the Court said. Invoking Justice Benjamin Cardozo, the Court said a judge "is not a knight-errant roaming at will in pursuit of his own ideal of beauty or of goodness." However, here "we have a Tribunal 'innovating at pleasure'," the bench said. The Court was hearing an appeal by the Damodar Valley Corporation (DVC) against the review order. items.title: Supreme Court initiates case based on lawyer's letter seeking contempt action against Kerala Congress for post against CJI
items.summary: A letter seeking contempt of court action against Kerala Pradesh Congress Committee (KPCC) over a social media post against Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant has been registered as a writ petition by the Supreme Court. The letter, written to the CJI by advocate Vineet Jindal on October 13, was registered as a civil writ petition on October 30. It is yet to be listed for hearing before a Bench. The controversial post against the CJI appeared on the official X handle of Congress Kerala on October 12. It read, "Dear Surya Kant, If law and order is not your domain, resign now. We will find your replacement who can handle it." The post was deleted soon after. In his letter, Jindal said the office of the CJI "cannot be treated as one whose continuance is subject to the approval or displeasure of any political organisation." The post, he said, raised questions as to whether it remains within the bounds of permissible political criticism or warrants consideration under the law relating to criminal contempt of court. items.title: A Fundamental Right
items.summary: With its new law that makes education a fundamental right with effect from April 1, 2010, India joins a small group of countries with such a statutory provision. All children in the 6 to 14 age group can exercise the right under the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009. An estimated one crore children who do not go to school now are expected to benefit.
